scenes.name: Landing: a next step for each observation
Describe visible litter without guessing a cause
Return to 120 minutes and three visits
Commit the plan to tracked responsibilities
Record the action and show the recheck gate
Assign and complete a follow-up recheck
Show completed follow-through in the workspace

captions.title: THE COORDINATION GAP
captions.caption:
A useful stream report deserves a clear next step.
What should a team check when it has just two hours?

captions.title: AN ISOLATED DEMONSTRATION
captions.caption:
Six fictional monitoring sites. Synthetic observations.
A private workspace for trying the complete workflow.

captions.title: 1 · RECORD THE PLACE
captions.caption:
Choose a monitored site and record the observation time.
The guidance keeps volunteers on safe public paths.

captions.title: 2 · DESCRIBE WHAT YOU NOTICED
captions.caption:
Report visible litter, clarity, and movement.
No one needs to guess the cause.

captions.title: 3 · KEEP THE UNCERTAINTY
captions.caption:
A short field note and an honest confidence choice.
Photos are optional support for human review.

captions.title: 4 · SUBMIT A USEFUL REPORT
captions.caption:
Review the details, then submit.
Every report in this workspace remains labelled as demonstration data.

captions.title: PRIORITY IS NOT A DIAGNOSIS
captions.caption:
Verification priority and evidence strength are separate.
This is a rule-based attention score, not a water-safety assessment.

captions.title: SHOW THE REASONS
captions.caption:
The score exposes its factors and the next question to answer.
Independent-looking accounts are not verified independent identities.

captions.title: ONE STREAM · CONNECTED LIVES
captions.caption:
Habitat, animals, and people remain part of the same decision.
Visual reports cannot identify pathogens or certify safe water.

captions.title: THE NEXT TWO HOURS
captions.caption:
Build a field plan from the time the team actually has.
Each visit includes an access allowance and observation time.

captions.title: LESS TIME · A DIFFERENT CHOICE
captions.caption:
Reducing the budget changes the selected work.
The planner chooses across distinct eligible sites.

captions.title: A REAL TRADEOFF
captions.caption:
At 120 minutes, three visits fit. Another concern must wait.
The selection maximizes the stated priority policy, not ecological outcomes.

captions.title: DEFERRALS ARE EXPLAINED
captions.caption:
Restricted sites and serious signs do not become volunteer visits.
The coordinator still confirms permissions and safe access.

captions.title: TURN A PLAN INTO RESPONSIBILITY
captions.caption:
Commit the reviewed plan.
Each selected visit becomes a task with an owner and a due date.

captions.title: HUMAN REVIEW
captions.caption:
The coordinator records a judgment before advancing the case.
The original evidence and the decision stay connected.

captions.title: RECORD WHAT HAPPENED
captions.caption:
A task is completed with a written result.
This fictional verification is explicitly labelled as a demo.

captions.title: ACTION IS NOT PROOF OF IMPROVEMENT
captions.caption:
A response can be recorded, but resolution remains blocked.
A completed recheck must provide the next piece of evidence.

captions.title: FOLLOW THROUGH WITH A RECHECK
captions.caption:
Assign the follow-up and record its findings.
A recheck does not certify water quality or contact safety.

captions.title: A DOCUMENTED LOOP, CLOSED
captions.caption:
A coordinator can now resolve the observation.
Report, review, action, and recheck form an accountable record.

captions.title: THE DECISIONS BEHIND THE CASE
captions.caption:
Authorship, time, and historical decision snapshots remain visible.
The complete retained audit trail can be exported.

captions.title: EVIDENCE THAT CAN TRAVEL
captions.caption:
JSON, CSV, GeoJSON, and an experimental FHIR R4 mapping.
Environmental Locations, Observations, Tasks, and Provenance — no Patients.

captions.title: MEASURE FOLLOW-THROUGH
captions.caption:
Count documented reviews, completed work, rechecks, and closed loops.
These workflow measures are not claims of improved water quality.

captions.title: A PRACTICAL PATH TO A PILOT
captions.caption:
Proposed customer: the monitoring coordinator. Volunteers contribute free.
Validate time saved and documented follow-through before making impact claims.
